transcript.text: f/f freezer keeps icing up bottom drawer wont shut proper, defrosted it 2wks ago already full of ice again. indesit

Since the ice returned so quickly after defrosting, this points to either a blocked drain preventing meltwater from escaping or a fault in the automatic defrost system. The most common and easiest fix is a blocked drain hole at the bottom of the back wall inside the freezer; if this is clogged with ice or debris, water pools and refreezes rapidly. Please check if that drain hole is clear by pouring a small amount of warm water into it to see if it drains away freely.
its a static freezer, no drain hole at the back that i can see. nothing automatic. any other ideas?

If there's no visible drain hole, the rapid icing is very likely caused by warm air leaking in through a faulty door seal, which then freezes instantly on the cold surfaces. Please check the rubber seal around the freezer door carefully: run your fingers along it to feel for splits or gaps, and look to see if any part has detached from the frame. If the seal looks damaged or loose, that is probably the cause; if it looks perfect, we need to investigate whether warm air is getting in elsewhere.
ok checked. bottom corner of the freezer door seal is split about 5cm and the hinge side bottom bit is flattened. paper test slides straight out there, grips elsewhere

[Heading: Likely cause: door seal]
The split seal and the way the paper test slides out suggests that warm air is leaking in; this moisture freezes instantly on the cold surfaces, which explains why the ice returned so quickly. Replacing the door seal should resolve the icing issue. To ensure you get the exact right part for your Indesit model, please check for a rating plate or sticker inside the fridge compartment (usually on a side wall near the salad drawer) and tell me the full model number.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
its a freezer seal not fridge, but ill go read the rating plate. model is IB55532W (indesit). what do i search for to buy the seal? is it push in or screwed, not sure yet

[Heading: Likely cause: door seal]
For the Indesit IB55532W, I cannot confirm a specific seal part number or whether it is push-fit or screwed in via my catalogue. Because this model appears to be an older unit that may no longer have standard replacement parts listed online, you should contact the manufacturer directly or visit their official spare parts website to check availability for your exact serial number. If they do not supply a seal, or if you are unsure about fitting it yourself, I recommend calling a qualified engineer who can source the correct part and fit it safely.
